data.title: Service Creation Not Monitored
data.summary:
Windows services were created on compromised hosts to run attacker code as SYSTEM at boot.
Creation generated no alert, and the services were not identified by any review.
data.description:
A service is durable persistence at the highest local privilege: it starts before any user
logs on, runs as SYSTEM, and restarts if it stops. Service creation is also a standard
remote execution technique, so the same event frequently marks lateral movement as well.

Detection is straightforward in principle. Service installation produces a specific event
with the binary path, legitimate creation outside deployment tooling is rare, and the
signal is low-volume. As with scheduled tasks, the obstacle is that the events are not
collected.

Services pointing at user-writable paths warrant particular attention, since that
combination is both a persistence mechanism and a privilege escalation path.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on service installation, excluding known deployment tooling by identity rather than
  suppressing the event.
* Review services whose binary path is user-writable or outside protected directories.
* Restrict remote service creation to administrative tiers and management hosts.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on service installation and review services in writable paths.
